newsitem.title: UK: Go-Ahead hits new heights, bid talk grows.
newsitem.headline: Go-Ahead hits new heights, bid talk grows.

text.p: Shares in bus operator Go-Ahead Group Plc rocketed to a record high on Friday with analysts saying the stock could be subject of bid talk after it won a key rail franchise on Thursday.
Go-Ahead shares powered to a high of 395 pence in early trade -- after yesterday rising 42p -- but eased back to trade 16p higher at 383-1/2 by 0947 GMT.

The company yesterday reported a 40 percent rise in pre-tax profits for the year to end June and said Victory Railway Holdings, in which it has a 65 percent stake, had won the Thames Trains Franchise.
"The stock is a bid target," said one transport analyst. "There are a few firms who wanted to get their hands on Thames Trains, but they lost out to Go-Ahead."
"All the bus companies are interested in getting into the rail business."
Analysts said that while Stagecoach, Firstbus and National Express could all have an interest in Go-Ahead, National Express would be the one not hampered by competition rules on local bus routes.
Analysts said a jump in Go-Ahead's pretax profits to 11.9 million stg from 8.5 million also supported the stock.
